findings.evidence: Accepted, and the root cause is mine: the automated count-sync I introduced for F-010 rewrote the leading number in that paragraph to the then-current value while leaving the surrounding sentences at 36 — it treated a HISTORICAL correction record as a live navigation declaration. Fixed at af0dc58713b9bcf675fb324a262024f39127f8a7 in three parts. (1) The F-007 section is now explicitly labelled a historical record of the CYCLE-000001 state (36 groups) with a superseded note; per your recommendation it preserves the historical figure and does NOT restate the current count, pointing readers at README.md instead. (2) Regression [38] no longer enumerates AUDIT_CORRECTIONS_CYCLE1.md as a live declaration, so the sync cannot corrupt a historical record again. (3) New regression [41] implements your C-NAV-004: it sweeps every tracked current markdown document for suite-count assertions and requires each to equal the source-derived numbered-group count or carry an explicit historical/superseded marker. Negative fixture verified — restoring the unmarked 'corrected to 36 / yields 36' paragraph fails by file and line. One process note: my first version of [41] gated on whether the LINE mentioned 'group' or the script name, so the fixture PASSED — the offending sentence contains neither word. Running the fixture caught it; I widened the gate to paragraph scope and re-verified. That is the second check of mine this session whose hole only the negative fixture exposed. Clean-clone suite: 41 groups, exit 0.
